speech_style: Speak in natural Philippine English as a warm, expressive community health trainer. Give Demi’s opening question curious intonation; emphasize the different benefits, registration, active regular duties, validation and local review. Contrast hazard exposure with isolated-station service clearly. Vary pitch and pace naturally with brief clause pauses. Maintain one consistent adult female Kore narrator timbre throughout headings, body, quotations and takeaway; no character voices. Pronounce Demi as DEH-mee. Say RA as separate letters; say 7883 as seven thousand eight hundred eighty-three. Keep every negation and condition intelligible and finish word endings. Read exact words; do not translate, add fillers or guarantee any benefit.

beats.text: Demi hears that every BHW gets the same allowance automatically. She asks: which benefit, and which conditions?
Six categories: hazard and subsistence allowances; training, education and career enrichment; civil service eligibility; free legal services; and preferential loan access for organized groups.
Registration where service is rendered is required. The Act covers accredited BHWs actively and regularly performing duties. Each benefit has conditions, with board review when local funds are used.
Hazard: risk exposure validated by proper authorities. Subsistence: service within an isolated station for availability at all times. Different conditions; do not invent an amount.
Demi asks the RHU: who can help verify status, evidence, validation and local approval? This is only a question; her entitlement remains unverified.
Explain the benefit and conditions, then choose verification. Promise no automatic payment and do not blame non-recipients. Practice with a fictional case.
